summary.text: Wesley Bell is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 1st District. A former public defender, Ferguson city councilman and St. Louis County prosecuting attorney, he defeated incumbent Cori Bush in the 2024 Democratic primary and again in the 2026 primary, and sits on the House Oversight and Armed Services committees.

paragraphs.text: Born November 5, 1974, and raised in northern St. Louis County, the son of a police officer and a civil servant; graduated from Hazelwood East High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Lindenwood University and a law degree from the University of Missouri-Columbia.

Began his legal career as a St. Louis County public defender, later taught criminology at Florissant Valley Community College, and was appointed a municipal judge in Velda City and municipal prosecutor in Riverview.
Managed the 2006 campaign of Republican Mark Byrne against Rep. Lacy Clay in Missouri's 1st District, which Byrne described as a favor to him despite their differing political views.
Was elected to the Ferguson city council in 2015, in the aftermath of the Ferguson protests.

Won the August 2018 Democratic primary for St. Louis County prosecuting attorney over longtime incumbent Bob McCulloch, and took office in 2019 as the first African American to hold the post; he served until 2025.
Assumed office in the U.S. House in January 2025 after defeating incumbent Cori Bush in the 2024 Democratic primary; won the 2026 Democratic primary over Bush with about 59% of the vote to her 37%.

Is assigned to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Federal Law Enforcement and Health Care and Financial Services subcommittees) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Strategic Forces and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees).
